title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: SSRF occurs when an application makes a server-side request to a destination influenced by an untrusted user, potentially reaching internal or otherwise restricted services.
indicators: user-controlled URL passed to an HTTP client
webhook or fetch endpoint accepts arbitrary destinations
redirects or DNS resolution can reach private address ranges
prevention: Prefer an allow-list of trusted destinations and protocols.
Validate resolved addresses and block loopback, private, link-local, and metadata ranges.
Restrict outbound network access and revalidate redirects.
source: OWASP Top 10:2025 A01 Broken Access Control (https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/); OWASP SSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html); MITRE CWE-918 (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html)
